sentences.text: Eopteranodon possessed a toothless skull featuring a large crest similar to that of Pteranodon.
A second species, E. yixianensis, was named in 2023, though its validity remains questioned by scientists.
The genus was named in 2005 by paleontologists Lü Junchang and Zhang Xingliao.
The type species of the genus is Eopteranodon lii.
A second specimen, D2526, described in 2006, possessed a larger wingspan than the type specimen.
In 2017, a phylogenetic analysis classified Eopteranodon as a member of the family Tapejaridae based on crest and limb proportions.
Some classifications place Eopteranodon within the family Chaoyangopteridae.
Eopteranodon lived between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago, spanning the Barremian to Aptian stages.
